greek: Ἐξῆλθεν δὲ Δινα ἡ θυγάτηρ Λειας, ἣν ἔτεκεν τῷ Ιακωβ, καταμαθεῖν τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἐγχωρίων.
hint: Dinah, Leah's daughter by Jacob, goes out to get to know the daughters of the people of the land.

notes.text: ἐγχώριος, *in* or *of the country*, and as a noun *a dweller in the land, inhabitant*: the noun sense heads it, as with ἡ περίχωρος at 13:10.
καταμανθάνω, *to observe well*, as at 24:21; the aorist infinitive of purpose.

reading: [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Δινα]] the daughter of [[name:Λειας]], which [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, begot, produced and yielded|τίκτω]] to the [[name:Ιακωβ]], [[to observe well|to observe well and examine closely, to learn thoroughly, to perceive and understand, to discover and find, to consider|καταμανθάνω]] the daughters [[of the dwellers in the land|of the dwellers in the land, of the inhabitants, of the ones in and of the country, of the ones according to the custom of the country|ἐγχώριος]].

names.gloss: (Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")
(Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: καὶ εἶδεν αὐτὴν Συχεμ ὁ υἱὸς Εμμωρ ὁ Χορραῖος ὁ ἄρχων τῆς γῆς καὶ λαβὼν αὐτὴν ἐκοιμήθη μετʼ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐταπείνωσεν αὐτήν.
hint: Shechem, son of Hamor the Horite and ruler of the land, takes Dinah, sleeps with her and humbles her.

notes.text: ταπεινόω, *to lower*, as at 15:13 and 31:50; the Greek has no word of force here beyond it.
[[flag]] The Hebrew reads *the Hivite*; the Greek has *the Horite*, as at 36:20.

reading: and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at|ὁράω]] her [[name:Συχεμ]] the son of [[name:Εμμωρ]] the [[name:Χορραῖος]] [[the ruler|the ruler and commander and chief and captain, the chief magistrate|ἄρχων]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] and [[having taken|having taken, having received, having taken hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] her [[was lulled|was lulled, was hushed to sleep and put to sleep, was lulled to rest and stilled and calmed, fell asleep, went abed and lay abed, slept, fell asleep and died, kept watch at night|κοιμάω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of her and [[lowered|lowered, lessened, disparaged, humbled and abased, made lowly and humbled|ταπεινόω]] her.

names.gloss: (Συχεμ, from Hebrew Šĕkem, "shoulder", the man who bears the city's name)
(Χορραῖος, from Hebrew Ḥōrî, usually connected with ḥōr, "hole, cave")

greek: καὶ προσέσχεν τῇ ψυχῇ Δινας τῆς θυγατρὸς Ιακωβ καὶ ἠγάπησεν τὴν παρθένον καὶ ἐλάλησεν κατὰ τὴν διάνοιαν τῆς παρθένου αὐτῇ.
hint: Shechem attends to Dinah's soul, loves the girl, and speaks in keeping with her mind.

notes.text: προσέχω, *to hold to*, as at 4:5; with the dative it is the whole of what English calls clinging.
παρθένος, *a maid*, as at 24:14; the word says her state, not her age.

reading: and [[held to|held to and offered, brought to, turned to, turned the mind to, gave heed to|προσέχω]] [[to the breath|to the breath, to the life, to the spirit, to life and death, to the ghost, to the departed soul|ψυχή]] of [[name:Δινας]] of the daughter of [[name:Ιακωβ]] and [[treated with affection|treated with affection and caressed and loved and was fond of, regarded with brotherly love, was well pleased and contented with, was content|ἀγαπάω]] [[the maid|the maid, the maiden, the virgin, the girl|παρθένος]] and [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[the thought|the thought, the intention and purpose, the notion and opinion, the intelligence and understanding, the meaning|διάνοια]] [[of the maid|of the maid, of the maiden, of the virgin, of the girl|παρθένος]] to her.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Συχεμ πρὸς Εμμωρ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ λέγων Λαβέ μοι τὴν παιδίσκην ταύτην εἰς γυναῖκα.
hint: Shechem asks his father Hamor to take the girl for him as wife.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Συχεμ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Εμμωρ]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[take|take, receive, take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] to me [[the young girl|the young girl and maiden, the young slave and courtesan|παιδίσκη]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a woman|a woman, a mistress and lady, a wife and spouse, a mortal woman|γυνή]].

greek: Ιακωβ δὲ ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἐμίανεν ὁ υἱὸς Εμμωρ Διναν τὴν θυγατέρα αὐτοῦ· οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἦσαν μετὰ τῶν κτηνῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ, παρεσιώπησεν δὲ Ιακωβ ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτούς.
hint: Jacob hears that Dinah has been defiled, but keeps silent until his sons come in from the plain.

notes.text: μιαίνω, properly *to stain, dye*, then *to defile*; the word is of staining, not of violence.
παρασιωπάω, one sense, *to pass over in silence*, as at 24:21.

reading: [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, knew by hearsay, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[stained|stained, dyed, defiled and sullied, tainted and defiled|μιαίνω]] the son of [[name:Εμμωρ]] [[name:Διναν]] the daughter of him; [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the sons of him were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of the flocks and herds|of the flocks and herds, of the single beasts, of the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]] of him [[in the plain|within, inside of, and by means of the plain, the flat, the plain flat open country|ἐν; πεδίον]], passed over in silence [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[until|until, till, while and so long as|ἕως]] [[of the coming|of the coming, of the going, of the going back and returning, of the being going to and intending, of the coming within a little of and being near|ἔρχομαι]] them.

greek: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ Εμμωρ ὁ πατὴρ Συχεμ πρὸς Ιακωβ λαλῆσαι αὐτῷ.
hint: Hamor, Shechem's father, goes out to speak with Jacob.

notes.text: The aorist infinitive of purpose, as at 34:1.

reading: [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Εμμωρ]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of [[name:Συχεμ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[to talk|to talk, to chat, to prattle, to babble, to say, to talk of, to speak, to chatter, to chirp|λαλέω]] to him.

greek: οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ ἦλθον ἐκ τοῦ πεδίου· ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν, κατενύχθησαν οἱ ἄνδρες, καὶ λυπηρὸν ἦν αὐτοῖς σφόδρα ὅτι ἄσχημον ἐποίησεν ἐν Ισραηλ κοιμηθεὶς μετὰ τῆς θυγατρὸς Ιακωβ, καὶ οὐχ οὕτως ἔσται.
hint: Jacob's sons come in from the plain, stung and grieved at the shameful thing done in Israel.

notes.text: κατανύσσω, *to stab, gouge*, in the passive of the mind, as at 27:38.
ἀσχήμων, *misshapen, unseemly*, the neuter as a noun; the Greek names the shape of the deed, not its guilt.
The future of εἰμί closing the verse: a rule stated, not a report of what was said.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near|ἔρχομαι]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the plain|of the plain, of the flat, of the plain flat open country|πεδίον]]; [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, knew by hearsay, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]], [[were sorely pricked|were sorely pricked, were stupefied and slumbered|κατανύσσω]] [[the men|the men, the men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]], and [[painful|painful and distressing, causing sorrow, causing pain and troublesome and vexatious and offensive|λυπηρός]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, to them [[very|very and very much and exceedingly and violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[misshapen|misshapen and unseemly and shameful, indecorous|ἀσχήμων]] [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[having been lulled|having been lulled, having been hushed to sleep and put to sleep, having been lulled to rest and stilled and calmed, having fallen asleep, having gone abed and lain abed, having slept, having fallen asleep and died, having kept watch at night|κοιμάω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of the daughter of [[name:Ιακωβ]], and not [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much|οὕτως]] will be.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: καὶ ἐλάλησεν Εμμωρ αὐτοῖς λέγων Συχεμ ὁ υἱός μου προείλατο τῇ ψυχῇ τὴν θυγατέρα ὑμῶν· δότε οὖν αὐτὴν αὐτῷ γυναῖκα.
hint: Hamor tells them his son Shechem has chosen their daughter with his soul, and asks for her as his wife.

notes.text: προαιρέω, *to bring forth from one's stores*, and in the middle *to take away first for oneself* and *to choose before, prefer*.
The dative of the soul, as at 34:3: the choosing is said to be done with it.

reading: and [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[name:Εμμωρ]] to them [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[name:Συχεμ]] the son of me [[took away first for himself|took away first for himself, removed out of his way, chose before and preferred, preferred to do, purposed and proposed to do|προαιρέω]] [[to the breath|to the breath, to the life, to the spirit, to life and death, to the ghost, to the departed soul|ψυχή]] the daughter of you; [[give|give, grant, provide, give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] her to him [[a woman|a woman, a mistress and lady, a wife and spouse, a mortal woman|γυνή]].

greek: ἐπιγαμβρεύσασθε ἡμῖν· τὰς θυγατέρας ὑμῶν δότε ἡμῖν καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας ἡμῶν λάβετε τοῖς υἱοῖς ὑμῶν.
hint: Hamor proposes intermarriage, daughters given and taken both ways.

notes.text: ἐπιγαμβρεύω, one sense, *to marry as the next of kin*: the Greek is the word of the levirate, not of marriage generally.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐπιγαμβρεύσατε, the active imperative.

reading: marry as the next of kin to us; the daughters of you [[give|give, grant, provide, give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to us and the daughters of us [[take|take, receive, take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] to the sons of you.

greek: καὶ ἐν ἡμῖν κατοικεῖτε, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἰδοὺ πλατεῖα ἐναντίον ὑμῶν· κατοικεῖτε καὶ ἐμπορεύεσθε ἐπʼ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐγκτήσασθε ἐν αὐτῇ.
hint: Hamor offers them the broad land to dwell in, trade in, and acquire.

notes.text: πλατύς, *wide, broad*; the feminine with γῆ, as the printed page has it.
ἐγκτάομαι, one sense, *to acquire possessions in a foreign country*: the verb says they would be foreigners.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐνκτᾶσθαι, the present infinitive, and puts ἰδού before ἡ γῆ.

reading: and [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to us [[dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), settle in and colonise, inhabit, settle and dwell, lie and be situate|κατοικέω]], and [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[wide|wide and broad, flat and level, broad-shouldered, flat, a street, the flat of the hand, salt and brackish|πλατύς]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you; [[dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), settle in and colonise, inhabit, settle and dwell, lie and be situate|κατοικέω]] and [[travel|travel, travel for traffic and be merchants and trade and traffic, import, make gain of and overreach|ἐμπορεύομαι]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] of her and acquire possessions in [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to her.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Συχεμ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα αὐτῆς καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῆς Εὕροιμι χάριν ἐναντίον ὑμῶν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν εἴπητε, δώσομεν.
hint: Shechem asks favour of Dinah's father and brothers, promising whatever they name.

notes.text: The aorist optative, first singular: the wish standing on its own, without ἄν.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds ἡμῖν, *to us*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Συχεμ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of her and [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the sons of the same mother|the sons of the same mother, the brothers, the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] of her [[may I find|may I find, may I find out, may I discover, may I get and gain|εὑρίσκω]] [[outward grace|outward grace, favour, loveliness, graciousness and kindness and goodwill, thankfulness and thanks and gratitude, a favour and kindness and boon, a gratification and delight|χάρις]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you, and which ever [[you may say|you may say, you may speak, you may declare, you may call by name, you may tell|λέγω]] [[we will give|we will give, we will grant, we will provide, we will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]].

greek: πληθύνατε τὴν φερνὴν σφόδρα, καὶ δώσω, καθότι ἂν εἴπητέ μοι, καὶ δώσετέ μοι τὴν παῖδα ταύτην εἰς γυναῖκα.
hint: Shechem will pay any bride-price, however great, to have the girl as wife.

notes.text: φερνή, *that which is brought by the wife*, the dowry; here it is paid the other way, by the bridegroom, as the Hebrew mōhar is.

reading: [[make full|make full and increase and multiply|πληθύνω]] [[that which is brought by the wife|that which is brought by the wife, the dowry and portion, the dower, the bridal gifts|φερνή]] [[very|very and very much and exceedingly and violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]], and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]], in what manner ever [[you may say|you may say, you may speak, you may declare, you may call by name, you may tell|λέγω]] to me, and [[you will give|you will give, you will grant, you will provide, you will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to me [[the child|the child, the son, the daughter, the grandchild, the boy and youth and lad, the girl and maiden, the slave and servant and man and maid|παῖς]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a woman|a woman, a mistress and lady, a wife and spouse, a mortal woman|γυνή]].

greek: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ τῷ Συχεμ καὶ Εμμωρ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ μετὰ δόλου καὶ ἐλάλησαν αὐτοῖς, ὅτι ἐμίαναν Διναν τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῶν,
hint: Jacob's sons answer Shechem and Hamor with guile, because Dinah has been defiled.

notes.text: δόλος, *a bait*, as at 27:35, where Isaac says the same of Jacob.

reading: [[gave answer to|gave answer to and replied, answered, answered charges and defended themselves|ἀποκρίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] to the [[name:Συχεμ]] and to [[name:Εμμωρ]] [[to the father|to the father, to the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of a bait|of a bait, of any cunning contrivance for deceiving and catching, of any trick, of a stratagem, of craft and cunning and treachery|δόλος]] and [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] to them, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[stained|stained, dyed, defiled and sullied, tainted and defiled|μιαίνω]] [[name:Διναν]] the sister of them,

greek: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς Συμεων καὶ Λευι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ Δινας υἱοὶ δὲ Λειας Οὐ δυνησόμεθα ποιῆσαι τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο, δοῦναι τὴν ἀδελφὴν ἡμῶν ἀνθρώπῳ, ὃς ἔχει ἀκροβυστίαν· ἔστιν γὰρ ὄνειδος ἡμῖν.
hint: Simeon and Levi say they cannot give their sister to a man with a foreskin; it would be a reproach.

notes.text: ἀκροβυστία, *the foreskin*, as at 17:11; the Greek word itself is unknown outside the Septuagint and what follows it.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits τὸ ῥῆμα.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to them [[name:Συμεων]] and [[name:Λευι]] [[the sons of the same mother|the sons of the same mother, the brothers, the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] of [[name:Δινας]] sons [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Λειας]] not [[we will be able|we will be able and capable and strong enough, we will be powerful and mighty, we will have influence, we will dare and bear, we will pass for, we will be worth, we will be equivalent to, we will signify and mean, we will avail|δύναμαι]] [[to make|to make, to do, to produce, to create|ποιέω]] [[the that which is said|the that which is said and spoken, the word, the saying, the phrase, the subject of speech and the thing, the verb|ῥῆμα]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]], [[to give|to give, to grant, to provide, to give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] the sister of us [[to a man|to a man, to a human being, to mankind|ἄνθρωπος]], which [[has|has, holds, possesses, keeps, dwells in and inhabits, holds fast, bears up against and supports|ἔχω]] [[foreskin|foreskin, circumcision, uncircumcision, the uncircumcised|ἀκροβυστία]]; is [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[reproach|reproach and censure and blame, disgrace, matter of reproach|ὄνειδος]] to us.

names.gloss: (Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")

greek: ἐν τούτῳ ὁμοιωθησόμεθα ὑμῖν καὶ κατοικήσομεν ἐν ὑμῖν, ἐὰν γένησθε ὡς ἡμεῖς καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ περιτμηθῆναι ὑμῶν πᾶν ἀρσενικόν,
hint: The brothers' condition: every male of Hamor's people must be circumcised, to become as they are.

notes.text: ὁμοιόω, *to make like*, in the passive *to be made like, become like*.
ἐν with the articular infinitive: the one construction where the article before an infinitive is printed here.

reading: [[in this|within, inside of, and by means of this, the nearer, what follows|ἐν; οὗτος]] [[we will be made like|we will be made like, we will be likened and compared, we will become like, we will be like|ὁμοιόω]] to you and [[we will dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|we will dwell in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), we will settle in and colonise, we will inhabit, we will settle and dwell, we will lie and be situate|κατοικέω]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to you, [[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[you may come to be|you may come to be, you may arise, you may be brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] we and you [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[the being cut|the being cut, the being clipped round about, the being pruned, the being cut off, the being cut off and hemmed in all round, the being curtailed of, the being cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] of you [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] male,

greek: καὶ δώσομεν τὰς θυγατέρας ἡμῶν ὑμῖν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν θυγατέρων ὑμῶν λημψόμεθα ἡμῖν γυναῖκας καὶ οἰκήσομεν παρʼ ὑμῖν καὶ ἐσόμεθα ὡς γένος ἕν.
hint: On that condition the two peoples will exchange daughters, live side by side, and be one race.

notes.text: οἰκέω, *to inhabit*, beside κατοικέω in the verse before: the simple verb, not the compound.

reading: and [[we will give|we will give, we will grant, we will provide, we will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] the daughters of us to you and [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of the daughters of you [[we will take|we will take, we will receive, we will take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] to us [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women|γυνή]] and [[we will inhabit|we will inhabit, we will occupy, we will dwell and live, we will be settled|οἰκέω]] [[beside|beside, alongside of, by, at, before, with|παρά + dative]] to you and we will be [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[race|race, stock and family, offspring and posterity, a clan and house, a tribe and caste, a breed, an age and generation, sex and gender, a class and sort and kind, genus|γένος]] [[one|one, a single one and one alone|εἷς]].

greek: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ εἰσακούσητε ἡμῶν τοῦ περιτέμνεσθαι, λαβόντες τὰς θυγατέρας ἡμῶν ἀπελευσόμεθα.
hint: If refused, the brothers will take their daughters and go.

notes.text: The articular infinitive of the thing heard; the article is not printed, as at 34:5.

reading: [[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may hearken|you may hearken and give ear to, you may hear, you may hearken to and give heed to|εἰσακούω]] of us [[of the being cut|of the being cut, of the being clipped round about, of the being pruned, of the being cut off, of the being cut off and hemmed in all round, of the being curtailed of, of the being cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]], [[having taken|having taken, having received, having taken hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] the daughters of us [[we will go away|we will go away, we will depart from, we will depart, we will depart from life|ἀπέρχομαι]].

greek: καὶ ἤρεσαν οἱ λόγοι ἐναντίον Εμμωρ καὶ ἐναντίον Συχεμ τοῦ υἱοῦ Εμμωρ.
hint: The terms please Hamor and his son Shechem.

notes.text: ἀρέσκω, *to make good, make amends*, and so *to please*, as at 19:8.

reading: and [[made good|made good and made up, made amends, pleased and satisfied and flattered|ἀρέσκω]] [[the words|the words, the language and talk, the sayings and statements, the speech and discourse|λόγος]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of [[name:Εμμωρ]] and [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of [[name:Συχεμ]] of the son of [[name:Εμμωρ]].

greek: καὶ οὐκ ἐχρόνισεν ὁ νεανίσκος τοῦ ποιῆσαι τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο· ἐνέκειτο γὰρ τῇ θυγατρὶ Ιακωβ· αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ἐνδοξότατος πάντων τῶν ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Shechem, most honoured in his father's house, loses no time, being set on Jacob's daughter.

notes.text: ἔγκειμαι, *to lie in*, as at 8:21; the imperfect of a state kept up.
The superlative of ἔνδοξος, *held in esteem*; the Greek says most esteemed, where the Hebrew says most honoured.

reading: and not [[spent time|spent time, took time and tarried and lingered and delayed and was slow, remained long|χρονίζω]] the youth [[of the making|of the making, of the doing, of the producing, of the creating|ποιέω]] [[the that which is said|the that which is said and spoken, the word, the saying, the phrase, the subject of speech and the thing, the verb|ῥῆμα]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]]; [[was lying in|was lying in and wrapped in, was involved in, was pressing upon, was urgent and insisting, was devoted to|ἔγκειμαι]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] to the daughter of [[name:Ιακωβ]]; he [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[most held in esteem|most held in esteem and honour and of the highest repute, most notable|ἔνδοξος]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] of the ones [[in the house|within, inside of, and by means of the house and abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|ἐν; οἶκος]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him.

greek: ἦλθεν δὲ Εμμωρ καὶ Συχεμ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὴν πύλην τῆς πόλεως αὐτῶν καὶ ἐλάλησαν πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας τῆς πόλεως αὐτῶν λέγοντες
hint: Hamor and Shechem go to their city gate and speak to its men.

notes.text: πύλη, the one wing of a double gate, as at 19:1: the gate of the city is where its business is done.

reading: [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near|ἔρχομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Εμμωρ]] and [[name:Συχεμ]] the son of him [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the one wing of a pair of double gates|the one wing of a pair of double gates, the gates of a town, the house-door, the nether world and hell, the entrance, the orifice, the entrance into a country through mountains and the mountain-pass, the narrow straits|πύλη]] [[of the city|of the city, of the citadel, of the country, of the body of citizens, of the state|πόλις]] of them and [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the men|the men, the men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] [[of the city|of the city, of the citadel, of the country, of the body of citizens, of the state|πόλις]] of them [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]]

greek: Οἱ ἄνθρωποι οὗτοι εἰρηνικοί εἰσιν μεθʼ ἡμῶν· οἰκείτωσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐμπορευέσθωσαν αὐτήν, ἡ δὲ γῆ ἰδοὺ πλατεῖα ἐναντίον αὐτῶν. τὰς θυγατέρας αὐτῶν λημψόμεθα ἡμῖν γυναῖκας καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας ἡμῶν δώσομεν αὐτοῖς.
hint: Hamor and Shechem commend Jacob's people as peaceable, with room in the broad land and daughters to exchange.

notes.text: εἰρηνικός, *of* or *for peace*; the adjective, not a verb of making peace.

reading: [[the men|the men, the human beings, mankind|ἄνθρωπος]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[of peace|of peace, for peace and peaceful|εἰρηνικός]] are [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of us; [[let them inhabit|let them inhabit, let them occupy, let them dwell and live, let them be settled|οἰκέω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] and [[let them travel|let them travel, let them travel for traffic and be merchants and trade and traffic, let them import, let them make gain of and overreach|ἐμπορεύομαι]] her, [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[wide|wide and broad, flat and level, broad-shouldered, flat, a street, the flat of the hand, salt and brackish|πλατύς]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of them. the daughters of them [[we will take|we will take, we will receive, we will take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] to us [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women|γυνή]] and the daughters of us [[we will give|we will give, we will grant, we will provide, we will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to them.

greek: μόνον ἐν τούτῳ ὁμοιωθήσονται ἡμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τοῦ κατοικεῖν μεθʼ ἡμῶν ὥστε εἶναι λαὸν ἕνα, ἐν τῷ περιτέμνεσθαι ἡμῶν πᾶν ἀρσενικόν, καθὰ καὶ αὐτοὶ περιτέτμηνται.
hint: The one condition: every male in the city must be circumcised, as the newcomers are.

notes.text: The perfect of περιτέμνω: the circumcision stands done on them, a settled state.

reading: [[alone|alone, left alone and forsaken and solitary, only|μόνος]] [[in this|within, inside of, and by means of this, the nearer, what follows|ἐν; οὗτος]] [[they will be made like|they will be made like, they will be likened and compared, they will become like, they will be like|ὁμοιόω]] to us [[the men|the men, the human beings, mankind|ἄνθρωπος]] [[of the dwelling in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|of the dwelling in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), of the settling in and colonising, of the inhabiting, of the settling and dwelling, of the lying and being situate|κατοικέω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of us [[so as to|so as to, as to, on the condition that, and so and therefore and consequently, as and as being, since it was|ὥστε]] [[to be|to be, to exist|εἰμί]] [[a people|a people, men, soldiers, a land-army, the common men, folk, Jews, Christians|λαός]] [[one|one, a single one and one alone|εἷς]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] [[the being cut|the being cut, the being clipped round about, the being pruned, the being cut off, the being cut off and hemmed in all round, the being curtailed of, the being cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] of us [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] male, [[according as|according as and just as, like as if and exactly as|καθά]] also they [[they have been cut|they have been cut and it stands so, they have been clipped round about, they have been pruned, they have been cut off, they have been cut off and hemmed in all round, they have been curtailed of, they have been cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]].

greek: καὶ τὰ κτήνη αὐτῶν καὶ τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτῶν καὶ τὰ τετράποδα οὐχ ἡμῶν ἔσται; μόνον ἐν τούτῳ ὁμοιωθῶμεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ οἰκήσουσιν μεθʼ ἡμῶν.
hint: The newcomers' cattle and goods will become the city's, they argue, if only the condition is met.

notes.text: τετράπους, *four-footed*, the neuter plural as a noun beside κτήνη in the same verse.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus writes the three members differently, and a corrector deletes the repeated τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτῶν.

reading: and [[the flocks and herds|the flocks and herds, the single beasts, the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]] of them and [[the things beginning|the things beginning and making a beginning, the things beginning to be and coming into being and arising and springing up, the things being in existence|ὑπάρχω]] of them and [[the four-footed|the four-footed, the quadrupeds, the four feet in length|τετράπους]] not of us will be; [[alone|alone, left alone and forsaken and solitary, only|μόνος]] [[in this|within, inside of, and by means of this, the nearer, what follows|ἐν; οὗτος]] [[let us be made like|let us be made like, let us be likened and compared, let us become like, let us be like|ὁμοιόω]] to them, and [[they will inhabit|they will inhabit, they will occupy, they will dwell and live, they will be settled|οἰκέω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of us.

greek: καὶ εἰσήκουσαν Εμμωρ καὶ Συχεμ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ πάντες οἱ ἐκπορευόμενοι τὴν πύλην τῆς πόλεως αὐτῶν καὶ περιετέμοντο τὴν σάρκα τῆς ἀκροβυστίας αὐτῶν, πᾶς ἄρσην.
hint: All who go out of the city gate listen, and every male is circumcised.

notes.text: The aorist middle of περιτέμνω: they had it done to themselves, not a passive.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads the singular εἰσήκουσεν.

reading: and [[hearkened|hearkened and gave ear to, heard, hearkened to and gave heed to|εἰσακούω]] of [[name:Εμμωρ]] and of [[name:Συχεμ]] of the son of him [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the ones going out|the ones going out, the ones going forth, the ones marching out|ἐκπορεύομαι]] [[the one wing of a pair of double gates|the one wing of a pair of double gates, the gates of a town, the house-door, the nether world and hell, the entrance, the orifice, the entrance into a country through mountains and the mountain-pass, the narrow straits|πύλη]] [[of the city|of the city, of the citadel, of the country, of the body of citizens, of the state|πόλις]] of them and [[cut themselves|cut themselves, clipped themselves round about, pruned themselves, cut themselves off, cut themselves off and hemmed themselves in all round, curtailed themselves of, cut themselves off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] [[the flesh|the flesh, the muscles, the body, man's nature generally|σάρξ]] [[of the foreskin|of the foreskin, of the circumcision, of the uncircumcision, of the uncircumcised|ἀκροβυστία]] of them, [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[male|male, the male sex, masculine and strong, mighty|ἄρσην]].

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ, ὅτε ἦσαν ἐν τῷ πόνῳ, ἔλαβον οἱ δύο υἱοὶ Ιακωβ Συμεων καὶ Λευι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ Δινας ἕκαστος τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀσφαλῶς καὶ ἀπέκτειναν πᾶν ἀρσενικόν·
hint: On the third day, while the men are in pain, Simeon and Levi enter the city safely and kill every male.

notes.text: πόνος, *work, hard work, toil*, and so *the consequence of toil, pain*; the Greek word is of labour first.
The adverb of ἀσφαλής, which the entry glosses *in safety, with certainty* and gives all the adjective's senses.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits the second οἱ.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[in the day|within, inside of, and by means of the day, the day-break, the time|ἐν; ἡμέρα]] [[to the third|to the third, to the third and finishing, to the day after to-morrow, to the day before, to the thirdly, to the sacrifice to the dead offered the third day after the funeral, to the third part|τρίτος]] [[when|when, sometimes|ὅτε]], were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the work|within, inside of, and by means of the work, the hard work and toil, the toil and labour, the bodily exertion and exercise, the work and task and business, the implements for labour and stock in trade, the consequence of toil and distress and trouble and suffering and pain, the anything produced by work|ἐν; πόνος]], [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] the two sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[name:Συμεων]] and [[name:Λευι]] [[the sons of the same mother|the sons of the same mother, the brothers, the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] of [[name:Δινας]] [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself|ἕκαστος]] [[the large knife|the large knife and dirk, the knife for cutting up, the short sword and dagger, the sabre and bent sword, the rasor|μάχαιρα]] of him and [[went in|went in, went into and entered, came into, came in, came upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state|πόλις]] [[in safety|in safety and with certainty, not liable to fall, immoveably, steadfastly, firmly, unfailingly, trustily, surely, certainly, safely and securely|ἀσφαλῶς]] and [[killed|killed and slew, condemned to death|ἀποκτείνω]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] male;

greek: τόν τε Εμμωρ καὶ Συχεμ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπέκτειναν ἐν στόματι μαχαίρας καὶ ἔλαβον τὴν Διναν ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ Συχεμ καὶ ἐξῆλθον.
hint: Simeon and Levi kill Hamor and Shechem with the sword and take Dinah from Shechem's house.

notes.text: The Hebrew idiom *by the mouth of the sword* carried straight into Greek; στόμα keeps its own first sense.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts τόν before the first Συχεμ and reads Δεινα.

reading: [[and|and, both and, and also|τε]] the [[name:Εμμωρ]] and [[name:Συχεμ]] the son of him [[killed|killed and slew, condemned to death|ἀποκτείνω]] [[in mouth|within, inside of, and by means of mouth, the mouth as the organ of speech, the mouthpiece, the face, the chasm and cleft|ἐν; στόμα]] [[of a large knife|of a large knife and dirk, of a knife for cutting up, of a short sword and dagger, of a sabre and bent sword, of a rasor|μάχαιρα]] and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] the [[name:Διναν]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the house|of the house and abode and dwelling, of the room and chamber, of the house of a god and temple, of the household goods and substance, of the household and family|οἶκος]] of the [[name:Συχεμ]] and [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth|ἐξέρχομαι]].

greek: οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ Ιακωβ εἰσῆλθον ἐπὶ τοὺς τραυματίας καὶ διήρπασαν τὴν πόλιν, ἐν ᾗ ἐμίαναν Διναν τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῶν,
hint: Jacob's sons fall on the wounded and plunder the city where their sister was defiled.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ gives *wounded man* and *corpse of one slain*.
διαρπάζω, *to tear in pieces* first, then *to spoil, plunder*.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[went in|went in, went into and entered, came into, came in, came upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the wounded men|the wounded men, the corpses of ones slain|τραυματίας]] and [[tore in pieces|tore in pieces, effaced, spoiled and plundered, seized as plunder|διαρπάζω]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state|πόλις]], [[in which|within, inside of, and by means of which|ἐν; ὅς]] [[stained|stained, dyed, defiled and sullied, tainted and defiled|μιαίνω]] [[name:Διναν]] the sister of them,

greek: καὶ τὰ πρόβατα αὐτῶν καὶ τοὺς βόας αὐτῶν καὶ τοὺς ὄνους αὐτῶν, ὅσα τε ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ ὅσα ἦν ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ, ἔλαβον.
hint: The brothers take the sheep, oxen and asses, in the city and in the plain.

notes.text: βοῦς, feminine in the accusative through the corpus, as at 18:7 and 32:8.

reading: and [[the things that walk forward|the things that walk forward, the cattle, the flocks and herds, the horses, the small cattle, the sheep|πρόβατον]] of them and [[the bullocks|the bullocks and bulls and oxen, the cows, the oxen, the kine and cattle, the ox-hide shields|βοῦς]] of them and [[the asses|the asses, the beasts of burden, the windlasses and pulleys, the upper millstones, the beakers and wine-cups|ὄνος]] of them, [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] [[and|and, both and, and also|τε]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the city|within, inside of, and by means of the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state|ἐν; πόλις]] and [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the plain|within, inside of, and by means of the plain, the flat, the plain flat open country|ἐν; πεδίον]], [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]].

greek: καὶ πάντα τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀποσκευὴν αὐτῶν καὶ τὰς γυναῖκας αὐτῶν ᾐχμαλώτευσαν, καὶ διήρπασαν ὅσα τε ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ ὅσα ἦν ἐν ταῖς οἰκίαις.
hint: The brothers take captive the people, their goods and their wives, and plunder city and houses.

notes.text: σῶμα, *the body*, as at 15:11; of persons taken alive, the word the Greek uses for slaves.
ἀποσκευή, *the removal and riddance*, and so *the baggage*, as at 14:12.

reading: and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the bodies|the bodies, the dead bodies and corpses and carcases, the living bodies, the bodies and any material substances, the whole bodies and masses|σῶμα]] of them and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the removal|the removal and riddance, the baggage, the household stuff, the ordure and filth|ἀποσκευή]] of them and [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women|γυνή]] of them took prisoner, and [[tore in pieces|tore in pieces, effaced, spoiled and plundered, seized as plunder|διαρπάζω]] [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] [[and|and, both and, and also|τε]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the city|within, inside of, and by means of the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state|ἐν; πόλις]] and [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the buildings|within, inside of, and by means of the buildings, the houses, the dwellings, the households and domestic establishments, the households and inmates of the house, the houses and families from which one is descended|ἐν; οἰκία]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιακωβ Συμεων καὶ Λευι Μισητόν με πεποιήκατε ὥστε πονηρόν με εἶναι πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν τὴν γῆν, ἔν τε τοῖς Χαναναίοις καὶ τοῖς Φερεζαίοις· ἐγὼ δὲ ὀλιγοστός εἰμι ἐν ἀριθμῷ, καὶ συναχθέντες ἐπʼ ἐμὲ συγκόψουσίν με, καὶ ἐκτριβήσομαι ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ οἶκός μου.
hint: Jacob rebukes Simeon and Levi for making him hateful to the Canaanites and Perizzites, few as he is.

notes.text: ὀλιγοστός, *one out of a few*; the superlative form of ὀλίγος, not a comparative of number.
ἐκτρίβω, *to rub out*, as at 19:13; the future passive of the man himself.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus omits πᾶσιν and reads ἐκτρίβομαι, the present.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

I [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], one out of a few I am [[in number|within, inside of, and by means of number, amount and sum and extent, mere number and quantity, a numbering and counting, the science of numbers and numeration and arithmetic|ἐν; ἀριθμός]], and [[having been brought together|having been brought together, having been gathered together, having been collected, having been convened, having been joined in one and united, having been received into a house, having been drawn together and narrowed and contracted, having been concluded and inferred|συνάγω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] me [[they will break up|they will break up and cut up, they will thrash soundly and pound well|συγκόπτω]] me, and [[I will be rubbed out|I will be rubbed out, I will be rubbed hard, I will be destroyed root and branch, I will be rubbed constantly and worn out|ἐκτρίβω]] I and [[the house|the house and abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|οἶκος]] of me.

(Φερεζαῖος, from Hebrew Pĕrizzî, usually connected with pĕrāzî, "villager, dweller in open country")

greek: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἀλλʼ ὡσεὶ πόρνῃ χρήσωνται τῇ ἀδελφῇ ἡμῶν;
hint: Simeon and Levi answer with a question: is their sister to be used as a prostitute?

notes.text: χράομαι, *to use*, as at 12:16; the aorist subjunctive in a question, of what is not to be borne.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: the ones [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly|ἀλλά]] [[just as if|just as if and as though, about|ὡσεί]] [[to a harlot|to a harlot and prostitute|πόρνη]] [[they should use|they should use, they should have and use, they should indulge, they should experience and suffer and be subject to, they should come to, they should live under, they should make use of, they should treat, they should be intimate with, they should be in need and yearn after, they should have in use and possess|χράομαι]] to the sister of us;
